settings.name_in_paper: Best fair (soft) intervention identification in a causal model under a cost budget
unmapped: Arms are K soft interventions P_k(V|pa(V)) on a node V of a known causal DAG; the learner knows all intervention conditionals and the conditionals P(X|pa(X)) of the children of the binary sensitive attribute S, enabling importance-sampling information leakage between arms
Goal is the best arm among E-fair arms (counterfactual fairness constraint |zeta_i^{s',s}|,|zeta_i^{s,s'}| < E), i.e. constrained / feasible best-arm identification; learner knows threshold E
Learner may also sample with chosen sensitive attribute (hard intervention on S) at arm-dependent costs; average cost must not exceed budget B
Observes S, V, pa(V), children of S and their parents, and Y after each pull
settings.definition_quote: The problem we consider involves a fixed budget $B$, and pulling arm $i$ incurs a cost $c_i$. ... we restrict our theoretical analysis to bounding the error probability of the problem defined as $e(B) = \mathbb{P}(\hat{k}(B)\neq k^\star)$. Here $k^\star$ is the best \emph{fair} intervention, which is defined as the arm that has the largest expect outcome among all arms that are $\mathcal{E}$-fair.

symbols.rho_star: problem-dependent constant max{log(20/Delta), log(12/Delta^{s'}), log(12/Delta^s)} combining outcome and fairness gaps
symbols.H_bar: max_{k != k*} rho_k^3 / (2^{-2 rho_k} v*(B,R*(k))^2), hardness constant
symbols.logbar_n: harmonic number sum_{i=1}^{n(T)} 1/i with n(T) = ceil(log2 log10 sqrt(T))

conditions: a best fair arm k* exists with |xi_{k*}^{s,s'}|, |xi_{k*}^{s',s}| < E

source.quote: Consider a problem instance with $K$ candidate arms. Suppose $K>1$ and there exists a best fair arm $k^*$ satisfying $\abs{\xi_{k^*}^{s,s'}},\abs{\xi_{k^*}^{s',s}} < \mathcal{E}$. ... The error probability of Algorithm 1 is bounded as $e(T,B) \leq 8K^2\rho^\star\exp(-\frac{T}{8\bar{H}\overline{\log}(n(T))})$

results.notes: Restated as Theorem 10 in appendix. Reward range not explicitly stated; bounded_01 inferred from the proof. v* is the LP value of the budget allocation.

symbols.n_T: number of phases n(T) = ceil(log2 log10 sqrt(T))
symbols.xi_star: min_k min(||xi_k^{s,s'}| - E|, ||xi_k^{s',s}| - E|), fairness margin
symbols.v_star: v*(B) = min over nonempty R of the budget-allocation LP value v*(B,R)

conditions: no fair arm exists: for every arm either |xi_k^{s,s'}| >= E or |xi_k^{s',s}| >= E

source.quote: Suppose that $K > 1$ and for all arms $k\in [K]$ either $\abs*{\xi_k^{s,s'}} \geq \mathcal{E}$ or $\abs*{\xi_k^{s', s}} \geq \mathcal{E}$. ... Then, the probability that the algorithm declares no fair arm exists is at least $$1 - 4 K n(T)  \exp (-\frac{(\xi^*)^2 T }{32 n(T)^3 \overline{\log}\left(n(T)\right)}v^*(B)^2),$$

results.notes: Stated as probability of correctly declaring no fair arm >= 1 - X; recorded as error probability <= X.
